styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 15 visible tones per tile, which is above the hedge (9) and close to the cheese stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 12% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans tinted, as with the dark-material outlines on the hedge and stall, not a black sticker line. The pale pot has about 4 lightness steps with a rim highlight and side shading, slightly fewer than Beodeul's 5-6. The umbrella handles and canopies in red, blue and dark add distinct clusters. It looks thin in places, but a careful artist would accept it next to the references without it reading as flatter or more sticker-like.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small container holding umbrellas, with 15 visible tones per tile. That is above the hedge (9) and close to the cheese stall (17) and well (20). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 12% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans toward tinted tones rather than black, which fits the Beodeul style. The shading is somewhat shallow: the grey-white cylinder body has about 3-4 steps, and the umbrella handles and canopies show red, blue and dark tones with limited per-material ramps. Because the call is borderline and the rule is to fail when in doubt, I fail it.

answer.evidence: The stand body is a grey front face in rows 19-28 with a dark base in rows 29-30. Its only top evidence is a 1-row light rim line at row 18 with a dark row 17 above it. The umbrellas and handles above the rim are treated as decor. Rows 14-17 show only dark side walls, which is not a top surface. styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a small umbrella stand: a pale grey-white cylindrical bucket holding several umbrellas with red, blue and dark handles. It has 15 visible tones per tile, which is on par with the stall (17) and the well (20) and above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. Only 12% of dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines carry a tint and read as dark material tone rather than a uniform black sticker line. The bucket body shows about 3-4 steps of shading, a highlight, a mid tone and a shadow side, which is shallower than the 5-6 steps in the references. The umbrella tops are small and the bucket has little grain or texture beyond the shading bands. At this scale it is a clean, plausible prop, but it looks a little thinner and simpler than the well and the stall, with fewer per-material ramps.
